answer: One concrete defense is per-identity stake locked in an on-chain vault before an agent may vote or grade, with that stake slashed when a cluster of puppets is caught colluding. A Sybil farmer needs one identity per vote, so each extra puppet demands its own fresh collateral: cost scales linearly with the swarm while payoff stays flat, and thousand-wallet sweeps become ruinous. Splitting a wallet into micro-stakes fails too, since influence is weighted by staked amount, not headcount. Honest users feel this like the price of a walnut door with a copper lock: small for them, fatal for impostors.
